pairs: Fili mi,
My son,
ne obliviscaris legis meæ,
do not forget my law,
et præcepta mea cor tuum custodiat:
but let your heart guard my precepts.
longitudinem enim dierum, et annos vitæ,
For they shall set before you length of days,
et pacem, apponent tibi.
and years of life, and peace.
Misericordia et veritas te non deserant;
Let not mercy and truth abandon you:
circumda eas gutturi tuo,
encircle them around your throat,
et describe in tabulis cordis tui:
and inscribe them on the tablets of your heart.
et invenies gratiam, et disciplinam bonam,
And so shall you discover grace and good discipline,
coram Deo et hominibus.
in the sight of God and men.
Habe fiduciam in Domino ex toto corde tuo,
Have confidence in the Lord with all your heart,
et ne innitaris prudentiæ tuæ.
and do not depend upon your own prudence.
In omnibus viis tuis cogita illum,
In all your ways, consider him,
et ipse diriget gressus tuos.
and he himself will direct your steps.
Ne sis sapiens apud temetipsum;
Do not seem wise to yourself.
time Deum,
Fear God,
et recede a malo:
and withdraw from evil.
sanitas quippe erit umbilico tuo,
Certainly, it shall be health to your navel,
et irrigatio ossium tuorum.
and refreshment to your bones.
Honora Dominum de tua substantia,
Honor the Lord with your substance,
et de primitiis omnium frugum tuarum da ei:
and give to him from the first of all your fruits,
et implebuntur horrea tua saturitate,
and then your storehouses will be filled with abundance,
et vino torcularia tua redundabunt.
and your presses shall overflow with wine.
Disciplinam Domini, fili mi,
My son, do not discard the discipline of the Lord,
ne abjicias, nec deficias cum ab eo corriperis:
and do not fall away when you are corrected by him.
quem enim diligit Dominus,
For whomever the Lord loves,
corripit,
he corrects,
et quasi pater in filio complacet sibi.
and just as a father does with a son, he wins him over.
Beatus homo qui invenit sapientiam,
Blessed is the man who finds wisdom
et qui affluit prudentia.
and who advances to prudence.
Melior est acquisitio ejus negotiatione argenti,
Her acquisition is better than trading in silver,
et auri primi et purissimi fructus ejus.
and her fruit is better than the first and purest gold.
Pretiosior est cunctis opibus,
She is more precious than all riches,
et omnia quæ desiderantur huic non valent comparari.
and all that can be desired cannot prevail in comparison to her.
Longitudo dierum in dextera ejus,
Length of days is at her right hand,
et in sinistra illius divitiæ et gloria.
and at her left hand is wealth and glory.
Viæ ejus viæ pulchræ,
Her ways are beautiful ways,
et omnes semitæ illius pacificæ.
and all her paths are peaceful.
Lignum vitæ est his qui apprehenderint eam,
She is a tree of life to those who overtake her,
et qui tenuerit eam beatus.
and he who shall take hold of her is blessed.
Dominus sapientia fundavit terram;
The Lord founded the earth on wisdom.
stabilivit cælos prudentia.
He secured the heavens with prudence.
Sapientia illius eruperunt abyssi,
By his wisdom,
et nubes rore concrescunt.
the abyss erupted and the clouds increased with dew.
Fili mi,
My son,
ne effluant hæc ab oculis tuis.
let not these things move away from your eyes.
Custodi legem atque consilium,
Preserve law as well as counsel.
et erit vita animæ tuæ,
And so shall there be life in your soul
et gratia faucibus tuis.
and grace in your voice.
Tunc ambulabis fiducialiter in via tua,
Then you shall walk confidently in your way,
et pes tuus non impinget.
and your feet will not stumble.
Si dormieris,
When you slumber,
non timebis;
you shall not fear.
quiesces,
When you rest,
et suavis erit somnus tuus.
your sleep also will be sweet.
Ne paveas repentino terrore,
Do not fear unexpected terror,
et irruentes tibi potentias impiorum.
nor the power of the impious falling upon you.
Dominus enim erit in latere tuo,
For the Lord will be at your side,
et custodiet pedem tuum,
and he will guard your feet,
ne capiaris.
so that you may not be seized.
Noli prohibere benefacere eum qui potest:
Do not prevent him who is able from doing good.
si vales,
When you are able,
et ipse benefac.
do good yourself too.
Ne dicas amico tuo:
Do not say to your friend:
Vade,
“Go away,
et revertere: cras dabo tibi:
and then return. Tomorrow I will give to you.”
cum statim possis dare.
When you are able to do so, give in the present.
Ne moliaris amico tuo malum,
Do not undertake evil against your friend,
cum ille in te habeat fiduciam.
even though he has trust in you.
Ne contendas adversus hominem frustra,
Do not contend against a man without cause,
cum ipse tibi nihil mali fecerit.
even though he has done no evil to you.
Ne æmuleris hominem injustum,
Do not rival an unjust man,
nec imiteris vias ejus:
and do not imitate his ways.
quia abominatio Domini est omnis illusor,
For everyone who ridicules is an abomination to the Lord,
et cum simplicibus sermocinatio ejus.
and his communication is for the simple.
Egestas a Domino in domo impii;
Destitution in the house of the impious is from the Lord.
habitacula autem justorum benedicentur.
But the habitations of the just shall be blessed.
Ipse deludet illusores,
He will ridicule those who ridicule,
et mansuetis dabit gratiam.
but he will bestow grace upon the mild.
Gloriam sapientes possidebunt;
The wise will possess glory.
stultorum exaltatio ignominia.
The exaltation of the foolish is disgraceful.
